note: Open defect backlog, machine-readable so test_scripts/daily_gate.py can order the day's queue. Extracted 2026-09-11 from the 'Known defects, deliberately unfixed' section of docs/v2/CONTINUE.md, which was last written at 9efa649 and is six commits stale. Anything marked verify:true may already be fixed by 9187abc, 88aa676, bdfb7af, 63d5b70 or 9e1dca0 — confirm by execution before working it, and close it here if it is gone. Set status to 'fixed' with the commit, never delete the row.

defects.what: The foundation-model comparison picks its baseline by substring-matching the uploaded FILENAME for 'off'/'organic', so a periodic crystal named e.g. offcut.cif is compared against MACE-OFF. That crosses two incompatible energy conventions (-1..-15 vs -100..-600 eV/atom) and the delta it prints is meaningless.
defects.howToVerify: Parse a periodic structure from a file whose name contains 'off' (e.g. public/demo/silicon.cif renamed offcut.cif) and check foundationModelFor() in lib/model-domain.ts returns MACE-MP-0. Also check an isolated molecule carrying an element outside MACE_OFF_ELEMENTS (e.g. a C10Fe cluster) returns MACE-MP-0, and that c-diamond.xyz (periodic, C only) returns MACE-MP-0.

defects.what: The validator is absent from the deployed container: mace-api/Dockerfile's build context is mace-api/, so `COPY . .` cannot reach ../test_scripts/. Hosted results report validation.status 'unavailable' — degrading correctly, but degraded. The live site runs without the scientific gate the repo advertises.
defects.howToVerify: Run a calculation against the hosted API and read result.validation.status.
defects.fixNote: Dockerfile's build context can't be changed without restructuring the whole deploy (HF Space root = mace-api/ contents copied flat by .github/workflows/deploy-hf-space.yml). Fixed at the deploy step instead: that workflow now also copies test_scripts/validate_calculation.py into the Space root, which is exactly the sibling path calculate.py's _load_validator() already checks as its second candidate. Verified locally by simulating the flat HF Space layout (calculate.py + provenance.py + validate_calculation.py in one dir): _load_validator() goes from (None, 'not found') to a loaded module. Not verified against the live hosted API since that requires a push to main, which this routine does not do.

defects.what: code.gitCommit is null in the deployed container because there is no .git in the image, so the live provenance manifest cannot pin the code that produced a result. NOMAD stamps nomad_version and nomad_commit into every public entry at build time; SimpleAtom only manages it locally.
defects.howToVerify: Read provenance.code.gitCommit on a result from the hosted API. Fix by baking the SHA in as a build arg.
defects.fixNote: Fixed in two places, because the runtime lookup cannot work in the image: provenance.git_info() now falls back to a GIT_COMMIT file written next to the module, and deploy-hf-space.yml writes that file from the SHA it is pushing. The same workflow was ALSO never copying provenance.py into the Space at all, so no change to that module could ever have reached production — that copy is added too (same defect class as D2). Verified by execution in a simulated Space layout with no .git and an empty PATH: gitCommit goes from null ('FileNotFoundError: ... git') to the exact pinned SHA, while dirty stays null because it cannot be checked after the fact. Two regressions checked: a real checkout still uses live git and still reports dirty=true, and an empty GIT_COMMIT still yields null with a reason rather than a fabricated SHA. NOT verified against the live hosted API — that needs a push to main, which this routine does not do.

defects.what: mace-api/main.py returns HTTP 500 instead of 400 for a rejected calculationType, so the hosted FastAPI path reports a server fault for what is correct input validation. The refusal itself works; only the status is wrong.
defects.howToVerify: POST {'calculationType':'phonon'} to the running FastAPI and read the status code.
defects.fixNote: Refusals raise ContractError with an HTTP status; FastAPI maps it (400/403/413/422/429). Verified in-process with TestClient and in CI docker-smoke.

defects.what: Geometry-opt trajectories contain a duplicated frame 0 with off-by-one step labels, so the result message and the trajectory it ships contradict each other.
defects.howToVerify: Run a geometry-opt and compare len(trajectory) against the step count in result.message.
defects.fixNote: The manual record_opt_step() before run() is gone: ASE's Dynamics.irun already calls observers at nsteps == 0. Labels are opt.nsteps. Regression test: test_science_regressions.py::test_d5_geometry_opt_records_each_step_once.

defects.what: Upstream computes stress on every call and SimpleAtom discards it; properties.pressure is declared in the type and never populated. Materials Project shows a unit on every value it prints — a declared field that is always null is the opposite of that.
defects.howToVerify: Run a periodic single-point and read properties.pressure.
defects.fixNote: properties.stress (Voigt, GPa) and properties.pressure (GPa, -trace/3) for fully periodic cells only; null otherwise (a molecule's 'volume' is the neighbour list's padding box; upstream #1684). Silicon at the CIF lattice under MPA-0: +1.81 GPa.

defects.what: lattice and properties.volume are declared non-nullable in TypeScript but the backend sends null for both on non-periodic systems. The type asserts something the API does not guarantee.
defects.howToVerify: Run a molecule (non-periodic) and read lattice and properties.volume against their declared types.
defects.fixNote: types/mace.ts: lattice and properties.volume are `| null`; phantom density and status 'timeout' removed.

defects.what: ASE's get_temperature() divides by 3N even with centre-of-mass momentum pinned, so reported MD temperature reads about 11 percent low for a 9-atom molecule. The MD chart shows it as-is, with no note.
defects.howToVerify: Run NVT at 300 K on ethanol and read the plateau temperature off the chart.
defects.fixNote: Temperatures are computed over the ensemble's degrees of freedom (3N for NVT, 3N-3 for NVE/NPT), recorded as params.temperatureDegreesOfFreedom. See D18 for the larger NVT error found while verifying this.

defects.what: The force-arrow scale silently differs between models — 0.82 vs 1.0 A per eV/A on the same geometry — so two results for one molecule render non-comparable arrow lengths with no indication of the change.
defects.howToVerify: Render the same structure under MACE-MP-0 and MACE-OFF and measure arrow length per unit force.
defects.fixNote: The scale divided by |F|max, so it belonged to the model: on the demo ethanol MP-0 and OFF (|F|max 1.62 / 2.04 eV/A) printed 1.0 vs 0.50 A per eV/A at 766x520, and the larger force drew the shorter arrow (1.62 vs 1.02 A). It is now set by the geometry alone (1 eV/A drawn at 0.45 of the span, rung-rounded, cap 5): both models print 1.0, longest arrows 1.62 vs 2.04 A, legend tick 131.9 px for both. The screen-space tip ceiling still applies, and when it cuts the scale the legend says so — at 291x291 both models read '0.50 A per eV/A (cut from 1.0 to fit the frame)'. Measured with a Playwright script on /calculate?demo=true, Structure tab; numbers in the 5985bee commit message.

defects.what: 21 interactive targets are under 44x44 and nav links are 17px tall, so the site fails the platform minimum touch target on mobile. Partly addressed inside the viewer; unaddressed elsewhere.
defects.howToVerify: Measure every interactive element's bounding box at 375px in the browser pane.
defects.fixNote: touch-target utility for icon controls; max-sm:/pointer-coarse: 44 px minimums in Button, Select, Input, Tabs; header/footer links. Hit test (9 points over a >=44x44 box) at 375 px: 0 failures on calculator, results, benchmark, shared result. Remaining by design: inline links in sentences (WCAG 2.5.8 exception); viewer toolbar is 32 px on fine pointers and 44 px on coarse (it sizes on the pointer); /docs sidebar not in this round's scope.

defects.what: Force arrows are drawn for hidden C-H hydrogens, leaving arrows with no visible atom at their base.
defects.howToVerify: Toggle Hide C-H with force vectors on and look for orphaned arrows. Commit 9e1dca0 touched exactly this area — check it first.
defects.fixNote: Fixed by 9e1dca0 (no arrow for an atom that is not drawn) but never run in a browser; verified by execution on 2026-10-21 for 5985bee: with Hide C–H on, MP-0 and OFF each draw 4 arrows, and every arrow starts on an atom that is still styled (0 orphaned), at 766x520 and 291x291. 5985bee also makes hidden atoms' forces still bound the arrow scale, so hiding no longer rescales the remaining arrows (MP-0 at 766x520: 1.0 -> 0.50 before, 1.0 -> 1.0 after).

defects.what: components/ui/card.tsx CardHeader is a bare grid with no explicit columns unless a CardAction child is present — the same unsafe pattern that caused the /calculate mobile overflow, one level deeper. ResultsSkeleton has it too, currently inert.
defects.howToVerify: Render a CardHeader with two children and no CardAction at 375px.
defects.fixNote: CardHeader carries grid-cols-1 explicitly.

defects.what: The green selection shell in the viewer is nearly invisible — delta-G of only +2 while R and B drop 13.
defects.howToVerify: Select an atom, screenshot, and sample the shell pixel against the unselected atom.
defects.fixNote: Not a tuning problem: with a transparent canvas, 3Dmol blends translucent shapes against its own white clear colour, not against the page, so the 0.62-opacity halo measured an effective alpha of about 0.04 (about 0.5 at 0.9); disabling AO or the outline changed nothing. The halo ring over the page measured (243,240,232) -> (235,235,228), so green fell 5. The shell is gone. The selected atom itself is drawn opaque in the accent green, 0.10 A larger (stick rep gets a 0.30 A ball). Same ring of pixels after: (29,56,31); atom centre (138,138,138) -> (76,148,81). Checked in ball-and-stick, stick and spacefill.

defects.what: ase.io.read() with no index returns the LAST frame of a multi-frame file while the UI previews the first, so a trajectory upload was computed on a geometry the user never saw.

defects.what: NPT used pfactor = 75*units.fs**2, omitting the bulk modulus ASE's docs require (ptime^2 * B): a barostat ~47x softer than intended.
defects.fixNote: MelchionnaNPT with pfactor = (75 fs)^2 * 100 GPa; barostat settings recorded in params.

defects.what: ASE's default Langevin(fixcm=True) subtracts the random kick's centre-of-mass part as P/(m_i N) per atom and rescales by sqrt(N/(N-1)), exact only for equal masses. NVT ethanol (MACE-OFF small, 300 K target, 2 ps) equilibrated at 417 K over 3N-3 DOF: every NVT run on a mixed-mass molecule ran ~39% hot.
defects.source: found by execution 2026-10-20 while verifying D8
defects.fixNote: Langevin(fixcm=False): 298.8 K. Isolated with plain ASE (independent of dtype and timestep) and a Bussi control. Test: test_d18_nvt_equilibrates_at_the_target_temperature. Worth reporting to ASE.

defects.what: Untrusted checkpoint deserialisation: a process-wide torch.load(weights_only=False) patch plus public custom .model uploads, and modelSize passed unvalidated to upstream loaders that download and unpickle any URL or path.
defects.fixNote: safe_load.trusted_checkpoints(): SHA-256 allow-list from contract.json, explicit weights_only everywhere else; sizes are an allow-list; custom models refused on hosted. Planted-pickle test: its payload never runs.

defects.what: A request for device 'cuda' on a machine without CUDA silently runs on CPU in every path, with no result.warnings entry and no requestedDevice. Measured on CLI (local + hosted profiles), FastAPI /calculate and /v1/jobs (both profiles), Next /api/calculate and /api/jobs (local mode), and the UI: params.device 'cpu', manifest.runtime.device 'cpu', warnings absent. The UI keeps 'CUDA (GPU)' selected, the 'What will run' ledger omits the device, and the timing reads '0.16 s compute' with no device; 'cpu' appears only inside a params string.
defects.evidence: SIMPLEATOM_PROFILE=hosted python mace-api/calculate_local.py public/demo/ethanol.xyz '{"calculationType":"single-point","modelType":"MACE-OFF","modelSize":"small","device":"cuda"}' → status success, params.device cpu, requestedDevice None, warnings None, manifest.runtime.device cpu (docs/v2/evidence/2026-10-28/device/)
defects.howToVerify: ADR-0031 confirmation tests: hosted → device_unavailable; local on CPU-only → warning + params.requestedDevice.

defects.what: Docs promise a CPU fallback when CUDA runs out of memory; no out-of-memory handling exists anywhere in the backend. The FAQ's OOM advice suggests a smaller model size, but the default MACE-MPA-0 is published in one size.
defects.evidence: grep -nE 'OutOfMemory|out of memory|OOM' mace-api/calculate.py mace-api/jobs.py mace-api/main.py → no output
defects.howToVerify: ADR-0031 §5: torch.OutOfMemoryError → cuda_out_of_memory, docs rewritten; grep the docs for 'runs out of memory'.

defects.what: Neither /capabilities nor GET /api/calculate reports devices, and the contract allows 'cuda' on the hosted profile although the hosted image pins torch==2.10.0+cpu, so the UI cannot know which devices work.
defects.evidence: TestClient GET /capabilities (hosted) → keys appVersion, profile, customModels, limits, models — no devices
defects.howToVerify: ADR-0031 §1: /capabilities.devices.available == ['cpu'] on a CPU-only machine.

defects.what: The docs tell users to change the MD seed to generate independent replicas, but the calculator has no seed input; only API callers can set it.

defects.howToVerify: Either a seed field (contract param seed, 0–4294967295) in the MD section, or the sentence rewritten to 'via the API'.

defects.what: The results 'Limitations and uncertainty' list is static: it shows 'MACE-OFF scope' on MACE-MPA-0 and MACE-MP-0 results and advises running 'multiple model sizes (small/medium/large)', though MPA-0 has one size.

defects.what: The validator's self-test (the gate called 'the scientific gate') runs MACE-OFF geometry optimisation in float32 and calls upstream mace_mp/mace_off directly, so `all_passed: true` says nothing about SimpleAtom's engine, and its geometry-opt test contradicts CLAUDE.md's float64-for-optimisation rule. Its Si test uses MACE-MP-0 small, not the default MPA-0.
defects.evidence: baseline gate: 'MACE-OFF ethanol geometry opt' energy_before -4221.59619140625 (exactly float32-representable: numpy.float32(x) == x → True)
defects.howToVerify: Self-test runs through calculate.run_calculation with the effective params; geometry-opt asserts params.precision == 'float64'.

defects.what: Stale facts in the harness docs: Matbench Discovery ranks are given as MACE-MP-0 34 / MACE-MPA-0 21; on 2026-10-28 they are 36 and 22 of 43. SUCCESS-CRITERIA says calculate_local.py exits 0 on refusal; v2.2 exits 1 (the JSON check is still the right one).
defects.evidence: WebFetch https://matbench-discovery.materialsproject.org/ (2026-10-28) → MACE-MPA-0 row 22, MACE-MP-0 row 36, '43 of 53 eligible models'; guard runs → '[exit 1]' with status error

defects.what: Local mode lets anyone who can reach the dev server run code as the developer: custom models are enabled by default in the local profile, `next dev` listens on all interfaces, and no route checks Origin, so a LAN peer (or, absent Chrome's Local Network Access prompt, a visited website) can POST a pickled `model` to /api/jobs, which becomes `--model-path` and is unpickled.
defects.evidence: Server leg executed: calculate_local.py --model-path <benign pickle> ran the payload. Network leg (LAN POST) not executed — PLAUSIBLE.
defects.howToVerify: Bind `next dev` to 127.0.0.1 in package.json, require a same-origin check on POST /api/jobs and /api/calculate, and make custom models opt-in (ALLOW_CUSTOM_MODELS) even locally.
defects.source: review subagent (code-review high + security-review), in-process probes under scratchpad/review/, 2026-10-28

defects.what: On the hosted path the synchronous calculate route (used by the benchmark and POST /api/calculate) sends no X-SimpleAtom-Client-IP, so every visitor shares one per-visitor key on the Space: while one visitor's benchmark runs, every other visitor gets 429. Regression of the S4/ADR-0023 per-visitor limits; /api/jobs forwards the IP correctly.
defects.evidence: grep -n 'headers' lib/server/backend.ts (calculateRemote) → backendHeaders() only (lead re-check); reviewer probe: two /calculate calls with one X-Forwarded-For → second 429
defects.howToVerify: Forward proxyHeaders(clientIp(request)) from calculateRemote; test that two client IPs run concurrently.
defects.source: review subagent (code-review high + security-review), in-process probes under scratchpad/review/, 2026-10-28

defects.what: The hosted per-visitor cap (30 requests/hour) is smaller than one benchmark the hosted profile allows, so a permitted benchmark fails part-way with 429s recorded as per-pair errors.
defects.where: mace-api/jobs.py (rate window); mace-api/contract.json profiles.hosted maxBenchmarkStructures; app/api/benchmark/route.ts:245-251

defects.what: With MACE_API_TOKEN unset (the case in production today), the hosted API is open to direct callers and X-SimpleAtom-Client-IP is client-chosen, so per-visitor limits can be bypassed by rotating the header; the header is honoured even though the docstring says proxy authentication protects it.
defects.evidence: reviewer probe (hosted, token unset): distinct X-SimpleAtom-Client-IP values each admitted

defects.what: Resource bounds leak: the `_submissions` table grows on every request, refused ones included, and uploads up to 30 MB are fully received and spooled before the 2 MB hosted cap or the 401 apply.
defects.evidence: reviewer probes: +500 entries after 500 requests; 30 MB body accepted then refused
defects.howToVerify: Prune _submissions by window on insert; reject on Content-Length before reading; authenticate before reading the body.

defects.what: Synchronous /calculate keeps running after the client disconnects and holds the single worker and the visitor's slot; its wait counts queue time, so a job that never started is cancelled with 504; a cancel during a step-less phase (single point) is not honoured and the job later reports 'succeeded'.
defects.evidence: reviewer probes: retry after disconnect → 429; queued job cancelled with 504; cancel → status succeeded
defects.howToVerify: Cancel the job on disconnect; start the sync deadline at job start; report 'cancelled' when a cancel arrives, even if the step completes.
defects.source: review subagent (code-review high + security-review), in-process probes under scratchpad/review/, 2026-10-28

defects.what: A geometry optimisation that converges on the step at which the time budget runs out (or stops before step 0) is labelled 'DID NOT CONVERGE … still above fmax' while reporting max force 0.0378 eV/Å below fmax 0.05.
defects.evidence: reviewer probe (ASE EMT, budget-stop at the converging step) → message 'DID NOT CONVERGE', max force 0.0378 < fmax 0.05
defects.howToVerify: Decide convergence from the final forces (max|F| < fmax, ASE's strict test) after any stop, and say which stop happened.
defects.source: review subagent (code-review high + security-review), in-process probes under scratchpad/review/, 2026-10-28

defects.what: 'Auto' precision resolves MACE-MP-family geometry optimisation from mace_mp()'s float32 default to float64 (ADR-0005 intends this) and records it in params, but adds no result.warnings entry, which CLAUDE.md requires for any override of an upstream dtype default.
defects.evidence: python mace-api/calculate_local.py public/demo/silicon.cif '{"calculationType":"geometry-opt","modelType":"MACE-MP-0","modelSize":"medium","maxOptSteps":5}' → params.precision float64, warnings None (lead re-run)
defects.howToVerify: Either add the warning, or amend the CLAUDE.md rule to exempt the documented auto policy — decide in ADR-0005.

defects.what: MACE-OFF energy-per-atom bands are wrong for ordinary O-rich molecules: the 'typical' band (−600 to −100 eV/atom) flags the water demo (−693.7 eV/atom) in the UI, and CO2 (−1711.7 eV/atom) falls below the enforced −800 floor so the validator says 'Check structure'. The model's own atomic reference energies already put water at about −690 eV/atom. The 2026-10-20 audit deferred composition-aware bounds for halogens only.
defects.evidence: golden sp_water_off energy −2081.1209 eV / 3 atoms = −693.71 eV/atom (lead check); critic: CO2 → validator warning
defects.howToVerify: Bounds from the model's own atomic energies (E − Σ E0(Z) per atom), or composition-weighted bands; regression test on water, CO2, CH2Br2.

defects.what: MD summary statistics mislead: 'drift' is last minus first total energy (NVE golden: +0.0009 eV, while the fitted drift is −4.6e-5 eV/ps, opposite sign), and is also reported for NVT/NPT where energy is not conserved; 'mean temperature' averages every frame including warm-up and carries no uncertainty (NVT reports 299.1 K vs an equilibrated 290.2 ± 18.6 K).
defects.evidence: sed -n 1342,1343p mace-api/calculate.py → 'drift = totals[-1] - totals[0]', 'mean_temp = sum(temps) / len(temps)' (lead read); critic block averages
defects.howToVerify: Fitted drift per atom per ps for NVE only; mean T over the post-equilibration window with a block-averaged standard error, and say which window.

defects.what: The pressure reported at the end of MD omits the kinetic (ideal-gas) term (ASE get_stress default), so an NPT run at a 0 GPa target reports 0.303 GPa of virial-only pressure; with the kinetic 0.482 GPa it is 0.785 GPa. The label does not say 'virial'. NPT trajectories also carry no per-frame cell, volume or pressure, so a user cannot see that an 8-atom NPT cell's temperature fluctuations (210 K spread vs 92.6 K canonical) are not canonical.
defects.where: mace-api/calculate.py:498 (atoms.get_stress(voigt=True)) and the MD result builder
defects.evidence: critic recomputation, md_npt_si
defects.howToVerify: For MD use get_stress(include_ideal_gas=True) or label the value 'virial'; record per-frame volume and pressure for NPT; warn below a minimum cell size.

defects.what: Parameters that had no effect are echoed as effective: friction is recorded for NVE and NPT, where nothing uses it (CLAUDE.md pitfall 8: echo the effective parameters).
defects.evidence: golden md_nve_ethanol params include friction (critic)
defects.howToVerify: Echo friction only for NVT.

defects.what: Docs nits: the Units page table gives stress in eV/Å³ while results and the same page's pressure callout give GPa; the silicon CIF comment says 2.3517 Å (a√3/4 = 2.3516); the optimiser message says 'at or below' fmax while ASE's test is strictly below.
defects.evidence: sed -n 55,62p app/docs/units/page.tsx → 'Stress … eV/Å³' (lead read)
defects.howToVerify: Correct the three strings.

defects.what: Catalog 'Silicon (diamond)' and 'Diamond (carbon)' are not diamond lattices: each puts the 2-atom primitive-FCC basis (0,0,0),(a/4,a/4,a/4) inside a CUBIC a×a×a cell, so the lattice is 4× too sparse and every atom is 1-coordinated. MACE-MPA-0 gives the catalog 'silicon' −2.758 eV/atom against −5.412 eV/atom for the correct cell (public/demo/silicon.cif), under a diamond label and next to an experimental cohesive energy. Si(111) bonds are ~8% stretched. Live in production since 092c796 (2026-02-09); the source comments say 'Verified'.
defects.evidence: lead re-run: catalog si-diamond → 2 atoms, V/atom 80.05 Å³, coordination [1, 1] vs ase.build.bulk('Si','diamond',a=5.43,cubic=True) → 8 atoms, 20.01 Å³, [4]*8; calculate_local.py on the catalog cell (MPA-0 medium) → E/atom −2.7579 vs silicon.cif −5.4125
defects.howToVerify: Use the 8-atom conventional cells (or FCC primitive vectors); fix the si-111 bilayer (0.784 Å intra, 2.351 Å bond); add a vitest asserting V/atom and coordination for every periodic catalog entry.

defects.what: A result is not pinned to the run that produced it: the dashboard filename, Share and 'Compare with foundation model' read live form state, so uploading another file after a run publishes the old numbers under the new filename as a permanent MACE Link, and Compare runs the foundation model on the new structure against the old result.
defects.evidence: read-only (PLAUSIBLE, high confidence): result is cleared only in handleCalculate
defects.howToVerify: Snapshot {files, params, filename, structure} at run start (lastRun) and feed the dashboard, share and compare from it; use result.params.modelType for isCustom.
defects.source: frontend review subagent (code-review high), 2026-10-28 — notes: review-frontend.md
